evidence.note: The lead rests on a tier-1 primary that was opened and read in full (anthropic.com/research/Claude-accelerates-protein-design), plus the wet-lab collaborator's own write-up and independent trade coverage. Two stories cite Bloomberg reporting that returns 403 to an automated fetch (Fractile, SK Hynix); both are handled under the rubric's blocked-primary rule — attested by a source actually opened (Tom's Hardware, SK hynix's own newsroom), confidence capped at medium, and the prose attributes the claim to Bloomberg's reporting rather than to a document read directly. Docked one point for those two, per the rubric.

Every figure carries its basis and the conditions that produced it — the lead does not report a single hit rate but distinguishes 26.7% and 22.6% (48-hour multi-target, up to 12,500 H100 hours) from 35.1% (24 hours per single target, up to 2,500 H100 hours each), which is the difference the vendor's own framing could have blurred. Unitree separates the 629% intraday peak from the 460% close rather than using the larger number as the headline figure.

Vendor claims are consistently marked as claims: the Fractile story states its 100x/90% figures are "company figures for hardware that does not yet exist in deployable form." Docked from 5 because two whyItMatters paragraphs (Unitree, Samsung) run long compound sentences that would read better split.

The lead is defensible as the day's most material story — an agent autonomously beating a competition field at protein design is a capability result, not a funding round — and it carries Anthropic's own caveat that a binder is "just the first step" toward a drug, so it does not read as a press release. Nothing here repeats Nos. 1-3; the Grok 4.6 brief is explicitly scoped to the Bedrock availability and pricing, since the model itself already ran as a brief in No. 2.

All seven beats are represented for the first time, including the new India beat (Sarvam/Nvidia). No company exceeds 2 of 11 stories. Anthropic appears in two (the protein lead and as Fractile's customer) but on unrelated news, and after two Anthropic stories in No. 3 the editor's note leads on the science rather than the company. Docked one point because Models runs 1 against a target of 3 — genuinely thin, and disclosed.
